summary: script copies a local script to the remote host and runs it through the shell, without needing Python. SSH forces a pty so stderr merges into stdout; quote paths with spaces; vaulted scripts are decrypted automatically.
questions: How do I run a local shell script on remote servers?
Why is stderr empty when using the script module?
Does the script module need Python on the target?
Can script run a vault-encrypted script?
Should I write a module instead of using script?

answer_card.title: Run local scripts remotely
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible.builtin.script` transfers a local script and runs it via the remote shell. No Python needed; works on Windows.
- SSH forces `-tt`, so **stderr is merged into stdout**. For separate streams, use `copy` + `command`.
- Quote paths with spaces; vaulted scripts are auto-decrypted.
- Encode non-UTF-8 output. Writing a real module is preferred.
